newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell adopts human rights as a guiding principle.
newsitem.headline: Shell adopts human rights as a guiding principle.

text.p: Oil group Royal Dutch/Shell on Monday published its revised business principles, incorporating respect for human rights for the first time.
In response to criticism by pressure groups, the principles require Shell companies "to express support for fundamental human rights in line with the legitimate role of business."
Two pressure groups with whom Shell has been in discussions welcomed the initiative.

"Amnesty and Pax Christi welcome the explicit support for fundamental human rights...The multinational redefines its former principle of abstaining from interference in political matters and no longer regards human rights as purely domestic politics," Amnesty International and Dutch Christian group Pax Christi said in a joint statement.
"Amnesty International and Pax Christi advocate this example to be followed by other multinational corporations," it added.
In the last two years, Shell has faced a barrage of criticism over its Nigerian operations and its plans, since abandoned, to dispose of the Brent Spar oil loading buoy in the north Atlantic.
Shell last revised its business principles in 1994, but has been in talks with a variety of pressure groups since last year.
Chairman Cor Herkstroeter, speaking on Monday, said that Shell companies should speak out when necessary.

"(Shell companies) do have the right to speak out on matters affecting their businesses and -- where they have something to contribute -- the community," he told an audience of business students at Erasmus University in Rotterdam.
He said Shell companies should ensure their behaviour matched their intentions.
His speech also stressed Shell's commitment to sustainable development.
